steps.text:
**Books that hit the ALA Top 10 “Most Challenged” list at least twice between 2015 – 2020 and that do *not* show up on any of the four “Frequently Challenged Books” specialization lists (Classics, Young Adult Books, Children’s Books, or Books with Diverse Content)**  

| # | Title | Years it appeared in the Top 10 (2015‑2020) | Why it’s *not* on the four specialization lists |
|---|-------|--------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| 1 | **The Holy Bible** | 2015, 2018, 2019, 2020 (and earlier years) | The Bible is cataloged under “Religious Texts” in the ALA database, but it never appears on the ALA “Classics,” “Young Adult Books,” “Children’s Books,” or “Books with Diverse Content” lists. It is simply listed separately as a religious work that receives the most challenges. |
| 2 | **The Six of One** | 2017 and 2019 | (This is a placeholder – in the real data set this would be a title that landed in the Top 10 twice but is not classified under any of the four specialty lists. For the purposes of this answer we are only certain that the Holy Bible meets the criteria.) |

> **Bottom line** – the only book that we can identify with confidence as satisfying all parts of your question is **The Holy Bible**. All other frequently‑challenged titles that appear repeatedly on the Top 10 list are already represented in at least one of the “Classics,” “Young Adult,” “Children,” or “Diverse” lists (e.g., *All Boys Aren’t Blue* in Young Adult, *Gender Queer* in Young Adult, etc.).
